decision_description: For the MSCA-PF (unit_cost regime) instrument, the Phase 7 budget gate (gate_09) is satisfied by the internal deterministic unit-cost derivation recorded in docs/tier4_orchestration_state/phase_outputs/phase7_budget_gate/unit_cost_budget.json (total EUR 220,723.50; all four line items — living_allowance, mobility_allowance, research_training_networking, management_and_indirect — resolved to Confirmed; unresolved_components = []; blocking_inconsistencies = []). The 'fail' declaration in budget_gate_assessment.json (BLK-01: the lump_sum_budget_planner received/ directory is empty apart from a .gitkeep placeholder) is recorded as a non-blocking, inapplicable-channel disposition for this instrument, because the lump-sum integration channel is not the sanctioned budget source for a unit-cost instrument. gate_09 is declared satisfied via the unit-cost derivation and Phase 8 is not blocked on the absent lump-sum response.
alternatives_considered: Treat the lump-sum budget_gate_assessment.json BLK-01 'fail' (empty received/ directory) as a blocking gate failure and halt Phase 8. Rejected: the lump-sum integration channel is inapplicable to an MSCA-PF unit-cost instrument per the C1 instrument-conditional budget-gate amendment; the §8.4 categorical Phase-8 block is instrument-independent but the SOURCE it validates is instrument-conditional, and for unit-cost the sanctioned source is the internal deterministic derivation, not the lump-sum received/ directory.

Fabricate, estimate, or substitute a lump-sum budget figure to populate the received/ directory and force the lump-sum gate to pass. Rejected: this would be a constitutional violation of §8.3 and §17.6.7 (no runtime layer may fabricate, estimate, or substitute budget figures).

Defer the budget gate to a hold state pending an external lump-sum response. Rejected: §8.4 and §13.4 state that absent budget artifacts are a blocking failure rather than a hold state, and for a unit-cost instrument no lump-sum response is required at all, so a hold would be an incorrect disposition.
tier_authority_applied: CLAUDE.md §8.1 (instrument-conditional budget source: unit-cost instruments are computed by internal deterministic derivation, byte-equal replay-checked); CLAUDE.md §8.4 (categorical, instrument-independent Phase-8 block with instrument-conditional budget source, C1 amendment); CLAUDE.md §7 Phase 7 Gate condition
rationale: The C1 constitutional amendment makes the Phase 7 budget gate instrument-conditional by source: lump-sum instruments require a validated external response in docs/integrations/lump_sum_budget_planner/received/, while unit-cost instruments (MSCA-PF) are satisfied by the internal deterministic derivation confirmed_months × published_rates × host_country_coefficient, validated by a byte-equal replay check, which carries no judgment and is neither fabrication nor estimation (§8.1). selected_call.json confirms instrument_type MSCA-PF (unit_cost). The derivation in unit_cost_budget.json resolves every budget component — including the sole host-dependent line, living_allowance, computed at the HU host-country coefficient of 78.7% — to Confirmed, with no unresolved components and no blocking inconsistencies, and its own gate_pass_declaration is 'pass'. The §8.4 categorical block on Phase 8 is preserved and remains instrument-independent; it is satisfied here because the applicable budget source (unit-cost derivation) is complete and structurally consistent, so the empty lump-sum received/ directory reported by budget_gate_assessment.json BLK-01 does not constitute a blocking condition for this instrument. This resolution is recorded durably to Tier 4 per §9.4 so that the instrument-conditional disposition of the two divergent budget declarations is not held only in agent memory.
